terms.name: Monophony
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: Follow the single tune: no second melody or harmonic backing enters.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Polyphony
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: At 2 seconds a second melody enters while the first continues. Follow each line separately.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Drone
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: The low note remains held while the upper melody changes.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Register
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: At 4 seconds the same melody repeats one octave higher, with the same scheduled gain.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Melisma
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: Follow a single sung vowel as its pitch changes through several notes. The course handout identifies this chant as highly melismatic; do not mistake one long held note for multiple notes.
terms.verification: Assigned official recording; source establishes highly melismatic setting, not a newly asserted local timestamp.

terms.name: Syllabic
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: Match successive sung syllables to their notes in A chantar; compare predominantly one-note-per-syllable delivery with any local multi-note ornaments rather than assuming every moment is syllabic.
terms.verification: Course handout establishes strophic form; performer upload confirms voice/vielle and verse texts. Exact verse-boundary times not independently assessed.

terms.name: Strophic
terms.source: Kendall Terminology Quiz packet; Medieval Music 1–2; Renaissance Music 1.
terms.listenFor: Compare the returning melodic phrase plan across successive sung verse texts over the full performance; allow varied ornaments and accompaniment, and do not infer whole-stanza repetition from one small recurring figure.
terms.verification: Course handout establishes strophic form; performer upload confirms voice/vielle and verse texts. Exact verse-boundary times not independently assessed.

terms.name: Homophony
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 1, page 1; Classical Music 1, page 1.
terms.listenFor: A foreground tune sounds above chords that change together.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Imitation
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 1, page 1 (Josquin opening).
terms.listenFor: At 2 seconds the lower part enters with the opening idea after the upper part has started.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Dissonance
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 2, pages 1–2 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: The middle pair is one semitone apart; compare its roughness with the wider, more stable outer pairs.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Cadence
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 2, pages 1–2 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: The final two chords move from dominant to tonic in C major. Listen for arrival, not just silence.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Monody
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 2, pages 1–2 (assigned course handout). Caccini is reference-only in the September 22 module.
terms.listenFor: Follow the solo singer carrying the text and compare the subordinate instrumental support; this includes accompaniment, unlike a single unaccompanied line.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Figured bass
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 2, pages 1–2 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Hear the supporting harmony and bass foundation, then consult the score to verify whether figures are written; a recording cannot reveal notation by itself.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Basso continuo
terms.source: Kendall, Renaissance Music 2, pages 1–2 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Trace the low foundation and accompanying harmony beneath the solo line; distinguish that supporting function from an exposed keyboard display.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Solo concerto
terms.source: Kendall, Classical Music 1 F. 21, page 1 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Compare piano-leading, orchestra-leading and shared passages across Mozart’s movement; do not require the soloist to play at every moment.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Cadenza
terms.source: Kendall, Classical Music 1 F. 21, page 1 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Look across the late solo passage for orchestral withdrawal and extended exposed display; verify its location before labeling a particular practice window.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Virtuosity
terms.source: Kendall, Classical Music 1 F. 21, page 1 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Identify a concrete demanding feature such as agile runs, rapid changes or wide range; describe the technique rather than merely calling the passage fast.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Galant style
terms.source: Kendall, Classical Music 1 F. 21, page 1 (assigned course handout).
terms.listenFor: Compare balanced phrase lengths and a question-and-answer relationship, then examine melodic foreground and harmonic clarity; one graceful moment cannot establish an entire style.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Meter
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: Count ONE-two with the stronger click returning every two beats.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Sonata form
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: Presentation at 0–10s, transformation at 10–14s, return at 14–22s, and an added close at 22–26s illustrate a simplified thematic plan. A real sonata also has a tonal design; this sketch cannot prove a course movement’s form.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Exposition
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: At 0–4s hear A; at 4–6s hear connecting material; at 6–10s hear contrasting B. This schematic presents themes before their transformation and return.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Development
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: At 10–14s fragments of A change pitch and shorten. Compare this transformation with the complete statement at 0–4s.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Recapitulation
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: A returns at 14–18s and B at 18–22s after their earlier presentation and transformation. Recognize the returning material; a real recapitulation also resolves the exposition’s tonal contrast.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Symphony
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: Follow the argument between orchestral sections in Beethoven without assuming a permanent concerto soloist; the genre needs the work’s identity as well as local sound.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Motif
terms.source: Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3; Classical Music 4; October 8 lecture draft (corroboration)
terms.listenFor: A short four-note idea returns at a different pitch level. Recognize the rhythm despite the changed pitches.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Word painting
terms.source: Exam guide p. 1; Renaissance Music 2 pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 2 pp. 1–4
terms.listenFor: Read the relevant text and connect a particular image with a specific musical gesture; for Era compare lower-voice death imagery with the higher-voice merciful-gaze passage after aligning the text.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Through-composed
terms.source: Exam guide p. 1; Renaissance Music 2; Baroque Music 2
terms.listenFor: Compare the music used for successive text sections across the vocal work; local repeated words or gestures can coexist with changing large-scale settings.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Beat / pulse
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Tap the evenly spaced underlying clicks.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Rhythm
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The steady clicks continue underneath notes of different lengths. Distinguish the beat from the note pattern.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Tempo
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The second four-beat group is faster than the first, while its grouping remains in fours.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Duple meter
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Count ONE-two with the stronger click returning every two beats.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Triple meter
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Count ONE-two-three with the stronger click returning every three beats.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Unmetered
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The note onsets are intentionally irregular; no regular strong-beat grouping is supplied.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Unison
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Two identical synthetic parts play the same pitches and rhythms; performers do not add independent lines.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Dynamics
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The second repetition uses the same pitches but a greater gain. Loudness changes without a register change.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Timbre
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The same note is presented with sine, triangle and sawtooth oscillators. Pitch and duration remain constant; the sound quality changes.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Major mode
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare C–E–G with C–E-flat–G: the third changes while the tonic remains C.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Minor mode
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: The second chord uses E-flat above C. Compare it with the first chord’s E-natural; sadness is not the test.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Consonance
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare the outer open-fifth pairs with the middle semitone pair. These are controlled sound contrasts, not universal emotional rules.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: Theme / subject
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow the longer opening idea and its contrasting answer. A theme can contain several smaller motifs.
terms.verification: Original scheduled sound events; explicit schematic rather than authentic repertoire.

terms.name: First subject
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow A at 0–4s; its repeated rhythm and contour identify a complete opening idea rather than only one note. It returns at 14–18s.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Second subject
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: At 6–10s B uses a different descending contour, contrasting with A. It returns at 18–22s; “second” means thematic role, not the second individual note.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Transition
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: At 4–6s the connecting ascending figure moves from A toward B. Hear its bridging role; in a real sonata it often also prepares a change of key.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Coda
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: At 22–26s a short added closing idea follows the returned themes. Its position after the principal return makes it a coda in this constructed sketch.
terms.verification: Original schematic A/transition/B/transformation/A/B/coda score, not a complete sonata movement.

terms.name: Concerto grosso
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow changes of prominence between Bach’s three-instrument solo group and the accompanying ensemble; total player count does not establish the design.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Concertino
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Track flute, violin and harpsichord as Bach’s identified solo group, individually and together; membership stays the same when a member temporarily supports another.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Ripieno
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare the fuller supporting string group with concertino-led passages; the harpsichord can also participate in the accompanying continuo role.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Madrigal
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Connect Monteverdi’s mixed-voice setting and changing textures with its secular text; polyphony alone cannot distinguish madrigal from motet.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Motet
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare sacred textual function with the secular madrigal rather than classifying by texture alone; use a documented motet, not O Sapientia chant, for a genre example.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Cantata
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow Strozzi’s soprano and instrumental accompaniment across contrasting text sections; solo voice with support is the performing configuration here, not a definition of every cantata.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Lament
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Read the grief and tears imagery, then compare how vocal pacing, dissonance and text setting contribute to expression; a minor sound alone does not establish lament.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Secular
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Use the love or grief subject matter of the supplied vocal text to establish non-liturgical context; no single instrument or texture proves secular function.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Sacred
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Read O Sapientia’s religious text and documented chant context; unaccompanied voices alone do not establish sacred purpose.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Soprano
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow Strozzi’s identified solo vocal part and its relative range against the accompaniment; loudness does not define the soprano range.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Alto
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Within Monteverdi’s documented mixed voices, compare a middle-lower vocal line with upper and lower parts; confirm part identity from score or credits when lines overlap.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Tenor
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare a middle male vocal range with the lower bass and upper voices; do not identify tenor solely from a single pitch in a shared range.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Bass
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Trace the lowest sung part within mixed voices, then distinguish that voice type from the structural bass function also carried by instruments.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Strings
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare bowed attacks, sustained tone and occasional plucked articulation across Bach’s string registers; verify identities through the ensemble credits.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Woodwinds
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare wind tone and articulation in Bach’s flute and the Classical orchestras; confirm identities instead of labeling every high tone flute.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Brass
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Use a documented orchestral passage to compare brass attacks and sustained tone with winds and strings; Bach’s specified ensemble contains no brass.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Percussion
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Check orchestral credits and locate struck rhythmic accents if present; Bach’s harpsichord jackrail sound is not evidence of a scored percussion part.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Keyboard
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Compare Mozart’s piano and Bach’s harpsichord for attack, decay and changing roles; the shared keyboard interface does not imply identical sound production.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Harpsichord
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Trace the plucked keyboard sound through supporting chords and exposed solo display in Bach; its instrument identity is distinct from its changing musical role.
terms.verification: Whole-work source-grounded observation task; exact audible cue location not independently assessed.

terms.name: Piano
terms.source: Kendall Listening Exam Study Guide pp. 1–2; Baroque Music 3 pp. 1–2; Classical Music 1 and 4.
terms.listenFor: Follow the principal solo keyboard line and compare its attack and orchestral interactions in Mozart; an orchestra-only passage remains part of the piano concerto.

terms.name: Flute
